_readme: This file is meant to be edited by hand, in GitHub, on a phone.
Every setting is checked when the site builds. If a colour choice would
make text unreadable, the build fails and tells you which pair and by how
much — it will not quietly ship a page nobody can read.
Run 'npm run build' after editing, or just commit and let Vercel do it.

organisation.name: Mas Oyama Karate New Zealand
organisation.tagline: Kyokushin karate in New Zealand since 1965
organisation._tagline: One line. Appears under the name in the header.
organisation._discipline: The art, as schema.org should label it. Judo, Taekwondo, Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu.
organisation._artName: What the pages call the art, which need not match the schema.org sport above. "Kyokushin karate" reads better in a page title than "Karate".
organisation._logo: The crest, as a file under data/media. Used in the header and on event banners until one is uploaded in the admin.
organisation._stripe: Belt colours for the thin stripe above the header and the footer (showcase layout). Leave it out for none.
organisation.footerLine: Mas Oyama Karate New Zealand · dojo throughout New Zealand and Japan
organisation.eventsIntro: National gradings, tournaments and camps. Individual dojo also run their own events — see your dojo's page.

vocabulary._readme: What this federation calls things. The platform serves any graded martial art, so none of these words are built in. A taekwondo body types Dojang, a kung fu body Kwoon, a BJJ body Academy, a Muay Thai body Gym. Leave a value out and the neutral word is used.
vocabulary._clubPlural: Some words do not take an s. Dojo is one of them.

_readme: Taken from your crest. Change any of them.
primary      buttons, links, the accent bar under headings
accent       dates and small highlights — DARK BACKGROUNDS ONLY
ink          headers, footers, dark sections
canvas       the page background
neutral      rules, dividers, quiet text
_derived: These are worked out from the ones above when the site builds.
Leave them out unless you want to override one:
primaryText, primaryTextStrong, primaryHover, inkSoft, canvasAlt, muted

_readme: Any two families from fonts.google.com. Pick from the list below or
type your own — spelt exactly as Google spells it.
Shippori Mincho / Zen Kaku Gothic New   Japanese, formal. Renders kanji.
Zen Antique / Noto Sans JP              Japanese, softer.
Bitter / Source Sans 3                  Steady, institutional.
Archivo / Archivo                       One family, heavy. Modern sport.
Libre Baskerville / Inter               Classic serif, neutral body.

firstNight.heading: What your first night looks like

items.title: Wear anything
items.text: Shorts and a t-shirt is fine. You'll train barefoot. Buy a gi later, once you know you're staying.
items.alt: Three instructors in seiza at the front of the dojo

items.title: Line up and learn the basics
items.text: Stances, blocks, counting in Japanese. You'll sweat, you'll get a few things wrong, and nobody will mind.
items.alt: Summer camp: kicking in line at sunset

items.title: Talk to the sensei after
items.text: Fees, training nights and where to buy gear. No contract on the night, no pressure to sign anything.
items.alt: Hanshi Doug Holloway performing mae geri

pathway.heading: Where it can take you
pathway.intro: Nobody starts thinking about a black belt. But the road is there, and it runs a long way.

steps.title: White belt
steps.text: Your first grading is usually within a few months. Small steps, close together.

steps.title: Coloured belts
steps.text: Grade with your own dojo, then at national gradings alongside every other dojo in the country.

steps.title: National tournament
steps.text: Fight at the national championships. Age and grade divisions, so you're matched fairly.

steps.title: Shodan
steps.text: Years, not months. Graded by a panel that includes 7th and 8th dan.

steps.title: Japan, and the 50
steps.text: Train at our Japan branch. Eight New Zealanders have completed the 50 Man Kumite.

photoBand.alt: Kaikan dojo members lined up in the hall, all ages and grades

lineage.heading: Sixty years of unbroken lineage
paragraphs: Hanshi Doug Holloway, 8th dan, set up the first Kyokushin karate dojo in New Zealand in 1965, after returning from Japan as a student of Sosai Mas Oyama.
Kyokushin means "the ultimate truth". It is taught here by people who learned it from the source.

spotlight.heading: Nine times in sixty years
paragraphs: Fifty consecutive full-contact fights, no rest. The 50 Man Kumite has been completed nine times in New Zealand — and most of the names on the board are the people who run MOKNZ today.

memberBand.heading: Already training with us?
memberBand.text: Renew, enter a grading, or show your MOKNZ card.

dojoPage.startAnyWeekText: You can start any week — there is no term to wait for.
dojoPage._showcase: Words for the showcase layout on every dojo page.

items.title: Turn up ten minutes early
items.text: Come in, say hello, and tell whoever's at the door it's your first time. No need to book.

items.title: Wear shorts and a t-shirt
items.text: You'll train barefoot. Bring a water bottle. That's the whole list.

items.title: Nobody hits you
items.text: You'll learn stances, blocks and how we line up. Contact comes much later, and only when you're ready.
